02 Executive Summary & Project Genesis

2.1 Operational Challenge

The Command Civil Engineering Department (East) [CCED(E)], stationed at the Sri Lanka Navy Dockyard, Trincomalee, oversees the planning, construction, renovation, and maintenance of naval shore infrastructure across the Eastern Naval Area (ENA). This operational purview encompasses multiple naval bases (e.g., SLNS Tissa, SLNS Vidura, SLNS Walagamba), specialized training academies, maritime piers, floating docks, residential quarters, and civil-military community projects.

Historically, official correspondence was handled through fragmented, paper-bound ledgers and independent word-processing templates. Key bottlenecks identified during operational audits included:

  • Serial Number Collisions: Inconsistent manual assignment of reference numbers across separate office desks (CCED Writer, Admin Office, Drawing Office).
  • Document Tracking Disconnects: Inability to rapidly determine the physical desk location or action officer for urgent naval files (the "Where is this letter?" problem).
  • Formatting Inconsistencies: Deviations from mandatory naval correspondence formatting prescribed in Book of Reference 7 (BR 7), resulting in document rejections and administrative delays.
  • Bilingual Language Complexities: Challenges in producing Sinhala-language minute sheets adhering to formal military terminology, correct rank translations, and standardized M01/M02 approval sequences.
  • Network Vulnerability: Heavy reliance on fragile cloud connections that fail during naval exercises, severe weather, or infrastructure blackouts.

2.2 System Vision & Strategic Solution

CMSys Documents is an enterprise-grade, dual-engine document workflow, military correspondence drafting, physical filing registry, and naval minute-sheet authoring platform. Developed from the ground up for high-tempo naval civil engineering environments, the system delivers an uncompromising balance of modern usability and robust military rigor.

Core Strategic Pillars
  1. 100% BR 7 Regulatory Compliance: Built-in structural guards enforcing naval precedence, security classifications, hierarchical paragraphing, and tone etiquette.
  2. Local-First Hybrid Resilience: Uninterrupted operational capability on isolated local area networks with automatic, asynchronous synchronization to cloud datastores.
  3. Zero-Build Architecture: 100% pure ECMAScript and pre-compiled styling requiring zero compilation toolchains (no Node.js/npm dependencies in production runtime).
  4. Bilingual Military Typography: Self-contained, offline TrueType fonts engineered for flawless Sinhala Unicode ligature shaping and standardized naval rank conversions.

03 Naval Operational Context & Domain Requirements

3.1 Command Hierarchy & Organizational Structure

The Sri Lanka Navy operates under a disciplined chain of command. In the Eastern Naval Area (ENA), technical civil engineering operations are centralized under the Command Civil Engineering Department (East), headed by the Command Civil Engineering Officer (East) [CCEO(E)], who reports administratively to the Commander Eastern Naval Area (COMEN) and technically to the Director General Civil Engineering (DGCE) at Naval Headquarters (NHQ), Colombo.

Strategic Command Level
Commander of the Navy (NHQ) • Director General Civil Engineering (DGCE) • Commander Eastern Naval Area (COMEN)
↓ Official Correspondence & Financial Directives
Operational Command: Command Civil Engineering Department (East)
Command Civil Engineering Officer (East) [Commander (CE)] • Staff Officer Civil Engineering (East) [Lt Cdr (CE)]
↓ Sectional Workflows & Registration Desks
Departmental Execution Sections
CCED Writer Section High-level command letters, NHQ submissions, external ministries, contractors.
Admin Office Section Personnel records, sailor administration, operational naval signals, internal routines.
Drawing Office Section Architectural drawings, structural blueprints, site surveys, Bill of Quantities (BOQ).
Minute Sheet Section Inter-departmental approvals, project expenditure requests, base maintenance estimates.

3.2 Regulatory Mandate: Naval Book of Reference 7 (BR 7)

The primary military regulatory constraint governing all official naval communications is BR 7 (Regulations for Naval Correspondence). CMSys Documents codifies these strict rules directly into software logic:

  1. Precedence Rules: Every correspondence must be explicitly marked with one of four military precedence levels: ROUTINE, PRIORITY, IMMEDIATE, or FLASH, dictating handling urgency.
  2. Security Classification: Mandatory headers and footers designating data sensitivity: UNCLASSIFIED, RESTRICTED, CONFIDENTIAL, or SECRET.
  3. Addressing Protocols:
    • To: Primary functional appointment (e.g., The Commander of the Navy). Individual names are strictly forbidden in formal naval addresses.
    • Through: Hierarchical routing channels (e.g., Through: The Commander Eastern Naval Area) ensuring chain-of-command visibility.
    • Attention: Specific staff officer designated for operational execution (e.g., Attention: Staff Officer Civil Engineering).
  4. Tone & Salutation Nuances:
    • Senior to Junior: Characterized by direct administrative phrasing ("You are requested to...", "I am directed to inform you..."). Complimentary close is generally omitted or standardized.
    • Junior to Senior: Subservient, formal phrasing ("I have the honour to submit...", "Submitted for your kind approval, please..."). Mandatory formal close: "I remain, Sir, Your obedient Servant".
    • Equal to Equal: Professional peer communication ("I have the honour to refer to...", "It would be appreciated if...").
  5. Paragraph Hierarchy: Sequential Arabic numeral enumeration (1., 2., 3.). Sub-paragraphs must follow alphabetical notation ((a), (b), (c)) and roman numeral sub-sub-paragraphs ((i), (ii), (iii)).

4.1 Architectural Style & Core Paradigms

CMSys Documents adopts a Local-First Service-Oriented Single-Page Application (SPA) architecture paired with an asynchronous Hybrid Dual-Storage Persistence Layer. This architecture was deliberately chosen over monolithic server-rendered frameworks or microservice containers to fulfill the unique security, reliability, and maintenance constraints of an operational naval base.

4.2 Architectural Design Principles

Design Principle Technical Implementation Operational Justification
Zero-Build Frontend Pure ECMAScript 6+ standard modules without Webpack, Vite, Babel, or NPM runtime dependencies. Static Tailwind CSS compilation. Air-gapped deployment readiness. Software runs instantly on any standard Apache web server without toolchain installs.
Local-First Resilience Primary execution against local MySQL database. Cloud writes occur via non-blocking cURL calls with strict 3-second timeouts. The system remains 100% operational even if the naval base loses satellite or maritime internet connectivity.
ACID Sequential Guarantee Reference generation utilizes database-backed sequence increments inside transaction blocks with explicit padding. Eliminates the catastrophic military risk of issuing duplicate official reference numbers to naval letters.
High-Fidelity Paper Simulation DOM elements sized precisely to standard A4 millimeter measurements with CSS Paged Media @page rules and zoom transformations. WYSIWYG accuracy. What the officer sees on screen prints with millimeter precision onto official naval stationery.

06 Frontend Architecture, Reactive State & Print Engine

6.1 Reactive State Architecture

Every UI action (tab transition, search query, minute paragraph addition, tone toggle) mutates this central state and triggers targeted re-renders without incurring the memory overhead of virtual DOM reconcilers.

07 Bilingual Typography Subsystem & Font Engineering

7.1 Offline Sinhala Unicode Architecture

A critical technical requirement for the Eastern Naval Command is the ability to author, preview, and print official minute sheets in Sinhala (à·ƒà·’à¶‚à·„à¶½) as mandated by Sri Lanka Government Official Language Regulations, while seamlessly switching to English for formal Naval Headquarters (NHQ) correspondence.

Standard browser font stacks frequently misrender complex Sinhala Indic ligatures, particularly kombuwa (à¶šà·œà¶¸à·Šà¶¶à·”à·€), kombu-dÉ™killa (à¶šà·œà¶¸à·Šà¶¶à·” à¶¯à·™à¶š), hal-lakuna (à·„à¶½à·Š à¶½à¶šà·”à¶«), and vertically stacked conjunct consonants (à¶¶à·à¶³à·’ à¶…à¶šà·”à¶»à·”). Furthermore, secure military networks operate behind air-gapped firewalls with zero access to Google Fonts CDN.

CMSys Documents resolves this challenge through an embedded offline font architecture declared in sinhala-fonts.css, housing 100% of required TrueType Font (TTF) binaries locally inside the fonts/ directory.

7.2 Automatic Naval Rank Sinhala Transliteration Engine

In official Sinhala minute sheets, naval ranks must not be written in raw English abbreviations (e.g., "Lt Cdr (CE)" or "MCPO"). Instead, they must be formatted using approved Sri Lanka Navy Sinhala designations. The client-side function convertRankToSinhala(rank) executes an automated linguistic transformation whenever a sailor or officer is inserted into a minute sheet.

08 Backend Architecture & RESTful API Specification

8.1 Request Pipeline & Action Dispatcher

The backend in api.php is designed as a centralized, high-performance RESTful API gateway. All incoming requests pass through a strictly defined execution pipeline:

  1. CORS & Pre-Flight Management: Automatic handling of HTTP OPTIONS requests with permissive cross-origin headers to support base-wide intranet clients.
  2. Input Body Ingestion: Dynamic parsing of raw php://input payload streams into strongly typed associative PHP arrays.
  3. Database Singleton Acquisition: Instantiation of Database::getInstance()->getConnection() utilizing persistent PDO connections configured with PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION and UTF-8 multibyte charset.
  4. Action Switching: Fast switch ($action) dispatcher delegating requests to corresponding domain services.
  5. Unified JSON Serialization: Standardized jsonResponse($data, $statusCode) enforcing JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE to preserve Sinhala script fidelity.

8.2 Complete RESTful API Endpoints Matrix

Method Action / Endpoint Parameters & Payload Summary Response Structure
GET ?action=documents section, flow_type, category, search, sort_by, id (optional single fetch) { success: true, data: [...] } • Returns array of document records with decoded position_trail.
POST ?action=documents JSON Document Object: ref_no, subject, flow_type, office_section, priority, etc. { success: true, id: "..." } • Inserts to MySQL and replicates to Firebase RTDB.
PUT ?action=documents JSON Document Object with valid id. Updates existing registry metadata. { success: true, message: "Updated" } • Synchronous dual-store update.
DELETE ?action=documents id query parameter or JSON payload containing id. { success: true, message: "Deleted" } • Removes from both MySQL and Firebase.
POST ?action=update_position doc_id, to_officer, action_status, remarks, officer_from { success: true, position_trail: [...] } • Appends new movement record to audit log.
POST ?action=save_outing doc_id, dispatch_mode, dispatch_book_ref, recipient, remarks { success: true, outing: {...} } • Transitions document to DISPATCHED state.

09 Database Architecture & Complete Data Dictionary

9.1 Entity-Relationship Conceptual Model

The database engine, ncw_ps_db, is engineered using MySQL 8.x with the InnoDB storage engine. All tables employ utf8mb4 encoding with utf8mb4_unicode_ci collation to natively support 4-byte Unicode characters (Sinhala, Tamil, emoji, and special military typographical symbols).

Core Document & Physical File Relationship Schema
registry_prefixes Defines sequence patterns: {YYYY}, {SEQ}
1 : N → document_registry
file_registry Physical Cabinets, Boxes, Volumes, Folios
1 : N → document_registry
document_registry Master Document Ledger • Inward / Outward
Houses position_trail (JSON)

10 BR 7 Naval Letter Studio & Correspondence Engine

10.1 Anatomy of a BR 7 Naval Letter

Naval correspondence strictly rejects civilian business letter conventions. The Naval Letter Studio codified within app.js and api.php enforces the structural composition mandated by the Sri Lanka Navy Book of Reference 7 (BR 7):

[SECURITY CLASSIFICATION & PRECEDENCE BANNER] — e.g., RESTRICTED • ROUTINE
LETTERHEAD BLOCK:
COMMAND CIVIL ENGINEERING DEPARTMENT (EAST)
SLN DOCKYARD, TRINCOMALEE
Tel: 026-2222384 / Ext 3144 • Email: cceoeast@navy.lk
REFERENCE & DATE BLOCK:
My Ref: CCED/NHQ/2026/0012
File Ref: CE/EAST/ADM/05
Date: 23 October 2026
ADDRESSING MATRIX:
To: The Commander of the Navy, Naval Headquarters, Colombo 01
Through: The Commander Eastern Naval Area
Attention: Director General Civil Engineering
SUBJECT: RECONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION NETWORK — SLNS TISSA
REFERENCES BLOCK:
(a) NHQ Letter NHQ/CE/05/2026/042 dated 10 September 2026
(b) COMEN Signal DTG 150830Z OCT 26
NUMBERED HIERARCHICAL PARAGRAPHS:
1. I have the honour to submit for your kind consideration and approval please that an on-site structural inspection was conducted...
2. The existing main distribution pipe network has developed severe corrosion...
3. The total estimated cost amounts to Rs. 1,485,000.00... Detailed breakdown is forwarded herewith at Annex A.
I remain, Sir,
Your obedient Servant,
(A B C SENEVIRATNE)
Commander (CE), SLN
Command Civil Engineering Officer (East)
ENCLOSURES / ANNEXES:
Annex A: Detailed Cost Estimate & BOQ
Annex B: Site Layout Drawing No. CCED/DRG/2026/045
DISTRIBUTION (COPY TO):
The Director General Civil Engineering, NHQ
The Command Logistics Officer (East)
The Commanding Officer, SLNS Tissa

10.2 The Dynamic Tone Engine

The system incorporates an automated tone transformer governed by the selected military relationship between the writer and the addressee:

Tone Mode Contextual Application Standard Opening Formula Complimentary Close Formula
junior
Junior to Senior		 Subordinate officer addressing higher naval authority (e.g., CCEO(E) writing to Commander of the Navy or COMEN). "I have the honour to submit for your kind consideration..." or "Submitted for your approval, please." "I remain, Sir,
Your obedient Servant"
senior
Senior to Junior		 Command authority directing subordinate base, ship, or workshop (e.g., CCEO(E) issuing tasking to OIC Civil). "You are requested to..." or "I am directed to inform you that..." Omitted entirely or standardized to "Commander (CE) for CCEO(E)".
equal
Equal / Peer		 Correspondence between equivalent command appointments (e.g., CCEO(E) to Command Logistics Officer). "I have the honour to refer to..." or "It would be appreciated if..." "Yours faithfully" or official signature block.

11 Bilingual Minute Sheet Studio & Dual-Minute Mechanics

11.1 The Dual-Minute (M01 & M02) Workflow Paradigm

In Sri Lanka Navy engineering operations, internal file movement is driven by Minute Sheets attached to the front of physical folders. A minute sheet typically requires a two-stage sequential endorsement:

  • Initial Minute (M01): Authored by the operational originator (e.g., Officer-in-Charge of Civil Works or Workshop Supervisor). Contains the technical background, site inspection observations, required materials, and formal engineering recommendations.
  • Secondary Minute / Endorsement (M02): Appended directly beneath M01 on the same physical sheet by the supervising authority (e.g., Command Civil Engineering Officer). Validates or amends the recommendation and submits it upward to the executive authority (e.g., Executive Officer or Base Commanding Officer).

12 Atomic Sequential Reference Engine & Physical File Registry

12.1 The Atomic Sequence Algorithm

Reference number collisions represent a severe operational liability in naval communications. CMSys Documents implements a thread-safe atomic sequence incrementation engine in api.php under case 'generate_ref':. 

// Architectural excerpt of atomic reference generation in api.php
$pdo->beginTransaction();

// 1. Fetch sequence rule with explicit Row Lock (FOR UPDATE)
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM registry_prefixes WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE");
$stmt->execute([$prefixId]);
$rule = $stmt->fetch();

$currentSeq = (int)$rule['next_sequence'];
$padLen     = (int)$rule['padding_length'];
$pattern    = $rule['prefix_pattern']; // e.g., "CCED/NHQ/{YYYY}/{SEQ}"

// 2. Format Sequence Token
$formattedSeq = ($padLen > 0) ? str_pad($currentSeq, $padLen, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT) : (string)$currentSeq;

// 3. Resolve Dynamic Date & Temporal Tokens
$replacements = [
    '{YYYY}' => date('Y'),         // 2026
    '{YY}'   => date('y'),         // 26
    '{MM}'   => date('m'),         // 10
    '{M}'    => date('n'),         // 10
    '{SEQ}'  => $formattedSeq
];
$generatedRef = str_replace(array_keys($replacements), array_values($replacements), $pattern);

// 4. Atomically Increment Counter
$upStmt = $pdo->prepare("UPDATE registry_prefixes SET next_sequence = next_sequence + 1, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = ?");
$upStmt->execute([$prefixId]);

$pdo->commit();
// Result: Guarantees zero sequence duplication across concurrent network requests

13 Hybrid Dual-Storage & Cloud Realtime Synchronization

13.1 Architecture of the Dual-Engine Persistence Model

To satisfy the dual requirements of absolute local durability and fleet-wide cloud synchronization, CMSys Documents employs a hybrid persistence topology. Local MySQL acts as the authoritative transactional database, while Google Firebase Realtime Database operates as the distributed cloud mirror.

Write-Through Transaction Execution Sequence
Step 1: Client initiates write (e.g., POST /api.php?action=documents).
Step 2: api.php executes parameterized SQL insert/update on local MySQL database (ncw_ps_db).
Step 3: If local SQL succeeds, api.php triggers an asynchronous cloud synchronization call via firebasePut().
Step 4: cURL transport executes with a strict 3-second timeout shield (CURLOPT_TIMEOUT = 3).
Step 5: If Firebase succeeds, the cloud mirror is updated. If Firebase fails or times out, the local operation still returns HTTP 200 SUCCESS, safeguarding local responsiveness.

13.2 Read-Fallback & Optimistic Caching Mechanics

Operational Condition Primary Data Source Fallback Mechanism User Impact & Recovery
Normal Operation (Local MySQL Active) Local MySQL ncw_ps_db None needed. Sub-millisecond response. Peak performance; full search and multi-column sorting capability.
Local Database Unreachable (Service Outage) Google Firebase Realtime Database cURL REST call fetches JSON object from /document_registry.json. Zero downtime for reading; client transitions seamlessly to cloud mirror.
Client Cold Startup (Initial Page Load) Static meta_cache.json Live metadata fetch via api.php?action=meta Instant UI rendering (0ms delay) of naval zones, workshops, and project titles.

14 Security Architecture, Threat Modeling & Air-Gapped Compliance

14.1 Threat Modeling & Mitigation Strategy

Threat Category Potential Attack Vector Architectural Mitigation in CMSys Documents
SQL Injection (SQLi) Malicious payloads injected into registry search queries or document edit fields. 100% of database queries utilize PDO Prepared Statements with strict parameter binding ($stmt->execute([...])). Direct SQL string concatenation is strictly banned.
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Malicious scripts stored in subject lines or letter paragraphs executing in reader browsers. Client-side rendering in app.js rigorously utilizes element.textContent for dynamic data and strictly escapes all user-supplied HTML entities prior to DOM insertion.
Supply Chain Compromise Malicious code injected via compromised external NPM packages or CDN scripts. Zero External CDN Calls. All stylesheets (Tailwind Static), scripts (vanilla ES6), and font binaries reside entirely on the local server filesystem.
Data Exfiltration Unauthorized network egress from secure base networks. System is engineered for 100% functional autonomy within air-gapped naval Intranets. Firebase integration is entirely optional and can be disabled via a single configuration flag.
Non-Repudiation Failure Denial of document custody or movement between operational officers. Immutable position_trail JSON audit ledger recording user, timestamp, sender, receiver, and specific action taken for every movement.

14.2 Departmental Access Isolation

The system enforces strict logical separation between the four major departmental desks:

  • cced_writer: Restricted to official command correspondence with NHQ, external ministries, and contractors.
  • admin_office: Confined to internal naval administration, sailor rosters, and classified naval signals.
  • drawing_office: Dedicated to architectural blueprints, structural plans, and BOQ engineering submissions.
  • minute_sheet: Restricted to inter-departmental civil engineering job minutes and base work requests.

17 Architectural Evaluation & Strategic Roadmap

17.1 Architectural Assessment & Lessons Learned

The deployment of CMSys Documents v2.4.0 marks a decisive operational milestone in the modernization of the Command Civil Engineering Department (East). Key engineering takeaways from system implementation include:

  • The Supremacy of Zero-Build Architecture: Avoiding heavyweight front-end build pipelines (such as Node.js, Webpack, or framework hydration) eliminated an entire class of deployment friction and security review hurdles common to military IT environments.
  • Dual-Store Resilience: Combining local MySQL with asynchronous Firebase replication proved ideal for naval shore establishments that experience periodic communication dropouts during adverse weather or joint maritime drills.
  • Typography as a Mission-Critical Feature: In multi-lingual military environments, accurate Unicode rendering of indigenous scripts (Sinhala) is not merely cosmetic; it is essential to legal clarity, command comprehension, and administrative validity.

17.2 Strategic Engineering Roadmap (Future Enhancements)

CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS `ncw_ps_db` CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
USE `ncw_ps_db`;

-- 1. Document Registry
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `document_registry` (
  `id` VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  `office_section` VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'cced_writer',
  `flow_type` VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INCOMING',
  `doc_type` VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'LETTER',
  `ref_no` VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  `sender_ref_no` VARCHAR(150) NULL,
  `sender_source_category` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `sender_or_recipient` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `date_letter` DATE NULL,
  `date_recorded` DATE NOT NULL,
  `subject` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `scope_description` TEXT NULL,
  `directed_type` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `directed_to` VARCHAR(128) NULL,
  `project_id` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `project_name` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `priority` VARCHAR(32) DEFAULT 'Normal',
  `security_class` VARCHAR(32) DEFAULT 'RESTRICTED',
  `present_position` VARCHAR(64) DEFAULT 'Received / In Registry',
  `action_officer` VARCHAR(128) NULL,
  `file_box_ref` VARCHAR(128) NULL,
  `file_no` VARCHAR(100) NULL,
  `folio_no` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `dispatch_mode` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `dispatch_book_ref` VARCHAR(128) NULL,
  `contact_person` VARCHAR(128) NULL,
  `contact_no` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `whatsapp_no` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `linked_estimate_id` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `linked_job_number` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `linked_signal_ref` VARCHAR(128) NULL,
  `position_trail` LONGTEXT NULL,
  `attachments_meta` LONGTEXT NULL,
  `status` VARCHAR(32) DEFAULT 'Active',
  `created_at` DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_at` DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  INDEX (`office_section`),
  INDEX (`flow_type`),
  INDEX (`ref_no`),
  INDEX (`file_no`),
  INDEX (`date_recorded`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

-- 2. Departmental Prefix Rules
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `registry_prefixes` (
  `id` VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  `office_section` VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
  `category` VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  `flow_type` VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'OUTGOING',
  `prefix_pattern` VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  `next_sequence` INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  `padding_length` INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 4,
  `separator_char` VARCHAR(8) DEFAULT '/',
  `description` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `is_default` TINYINT(1) DEFAULT 0,
  `updated_at` DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  INDEX (`office_section`),
  INDEX (`category`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

-- 3. File Registry
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `file_registry` (
  `id` VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  `file_no` VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  `subject` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `office_section` VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'cced_writer',
  `category` VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT 'General',
  `file_box_ref` VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT '',
  `cabinet_location` VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT '',
  `current_volume` VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'Vol 1',
  `total_folios` INT DEFAULT 0,
  `status` VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'Active',
  `remarks` TEXT NULL,
  `created_at` TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_at` TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  UNIQUE KEY `idx_file_no_sec` (`file_no`, `office_section`),
  INDEX (`office_section`),
  INDEX (`status`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
